Department of the Air Force: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition

CUI

VI. Integrated Market Analysis and Efforts to Solicit Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(6), (8), and (10)): The Government conducted market research for the follow-on award that was delayed as described above. Additional market research was not conducted. The current market research report identified no other existing contract vehicles which would afford a competitive acquisition in the time frame necessary. Competing this requirement in the current time frame would additionally lead to a lapse in services, putting mission support in jeopardy, as detailed above. VII. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost (RFO 6.104-1(a)(7)): The Contracting Officer is responsible for evaluating, determining, and documenting the anticipated contract cost/price is fair and reasonable in accordance with RFO Subpart 15.4, Contract Pricing. VIII. Any Other Facts Supporting the Justification (RFO 6.104-1(a)(9)): As the prior N00244-21-F-3022 contract was determined to be fair and reasonable, we are asking the contractor for proposals with escalated costs based on Option Year Four, rather than a brand new proposal. By comparing prices for the 12-month extension with prices paid during the previous option year, we will then utilize additional proposal analysis techniques under FAR 15.404-1(b)(2)(ii), "Comparison of the proposed prices to historical prices paid," to determine a fair and reasonable price. IX. Actions to Overcome Barriers to Competition (RFO 6.104-1(a)(11): There are no other actions planned to remove or overcome any barriers. A follow-on to this requirement is being completed on the General Services Administration (GSA) One Acquisition Solution Integrated Services (OASIS+) Small Business (SB) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Contract Vehicle.
